A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same information-estimation and IDEAL research despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original microscopy analyses, lensless imaging simulations, estimator-validation experiments, and snapshot 3D microscope optimization results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical analyses and reports additional color-filter design and simulated black hole imaging results.

M1.justification: The information estimator and decoder-free IDEAL objective remain intact. V2 adapts IDEAL to discrete color-filter selection using a temperature-scheduled softmax (Methods, Eq. 50), replacing continuous microlens optimization. The full Gaussian estimator already appeared in v1's supplementary experiments; its expanded documentation does not establish a new estimator.

E1.justification: V2 adds color reconstruction and filter design using Gehler-Shi images, plus black hole reconstruction using synthetic M87-like objects and telescope configurations. The fluorescent lung-volume experiments and snapshot 3D microscope optimization are removed throughout. BSCCM microscopy, CIFAR10 lensless imaging, MNIST, and the simplified simulations remain.

E2.justification: V1's direct comparison between IDEAL and end-to-end Fourier DiffuserScope optimization disappears. V2 introduces comparisons among Bayer, random RGBW, and Chakrabarti-learned color-filter designs (Fig. 3a), without an equivalent direct IDEAL-versus-end-to-end comparison. The three Gaussian/PixelCNN estimator families and the lensless encoder comparators were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The added applications introduce new dataset splits, noise models, and reconstruction protocols. Retained lensless deconvolution changes from reporting errors across 60,000 CIFAR10 images to a 1,500-image test set paired with information-estimation measurements, and adds PSNR and SSIM. Microscopy prediction changes from a median across replicates to selecting the best prediction performance.

E4.justification: V2 extends existing validation with fixed-versus-random patch sampling comparisons (Fig. S15), measured training times (Fig. S16), and checks across reconstruction metrics (Fig. S19). Existing patch-size, Gaussian-misspecification, noise-estimation, background-information, and classification analyses remain; their relocation or redrawing is not new analysis.

E5.justification: Existing bootstrap and repeated-run reporting is revised: many 90% intervals become 95%, lensless information-estimation replicates change from five to four, and microscopy replicates from eleven to fifteen. V2 expands bootstrap details and reports runtime standard deviations, but removes confidence bands from the 1D sweeps and classification plot. Its Fig. S21 specifies five classification networks while Methods still specifies ten, leaving that count unresolved.

E6.justification: New color-filter, telescope-configuration, and CFA optimization results replace the 3D microscopy results and quantitative IDEAL/end-to-end comparison. Retained results also change substantively: single-delta objects rank highest in v1's 1D sweeps (Fig. S5b), whereas eight-delta objects rank highest in v2 (Fig. S6b). Revised experimental protocols prevent interpreting updated scores generally as matched-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the cross-entropy identity from DKL(p_theta || p) in v1 Eq. 26 to DKL(p || p_theta) in Eq. 31. It also expands the conditional-expectation derivation in Eqs. 10–12. The principal information-theoretic framework, two-point analysis, and estimation-theory connections remain.

C1.justification: Information estimation and decoder-independent design remain the central contributions. However, v2 withdraws v1's claims that IDEAL outperforms end-to-end optimization while converging 3–4 times faster and using less GPU memory. Its Discussion presents the design results as initial evidence and explicitly leaves comprehensive comparison to future work.

C2.justification: Existing task-specific-information and calibration limitations are retained and refined. V2 explains estimator differences through fixed versus random patch sampling, discusses when specialized design methods are preferable, and attributes part of the single-LED prediction mismatch to system-derived information. V1's loss-landscape explanation for IDEAL's comparative superiority is removed.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands implementation disclosure, including Gaussian regularization, PixelCNN layer and mixture-component specifications, normalization, JAX/Flax, GPU hardware, and timing information. Detailed CFA and radio-imaging procedures replace the removed 3D implementation, while the earlier patching-strategy discussion is shortened. A project website and video link are added; the existing code repository remains.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands engagement with historical and task-specific information-based imaging research, including work by Huck, Fales, Neifeld, and Ashok. It more explicitly situates the probabilistic model within established analyses and adds substantial color-filter and radio-interferometry literature. References associated with the removed 3D demonstration and some earlier discussion are deleted.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, Results narrative, and Discussion are extensively rewritten. Estimator formulation now precedes the two-point example, explanatory material moves into the supplement, and Methods is reorganized by model and application. The supplement gains a contents section and consolidates the comparisons with other frameworks.

P2.justification: Main figures are substantially redesigned: material from v1 Fig. 1 is redistributed across v2 Figs. 1, 2, and S2, and the supplementary optimal-classifier curve is promoted into Fig. 2. Application Fig. 3 and IDEAL Fig. 4 are rebuilt. Supplementary plots receive extensive layout, axis, legend, and panel changes, including new runtime and multiple-metric displays.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical correctness through the KL correction, strengthens research positioning, and makes the framework clearer and better documented. Added applications and targeted validation improve its practical support. These gains are tempered by losing the direct IDEAL comparison, replacing median microscopy performance with best-run summaries, and introducing the five-versus-ten classification-run inconsistency, limiting the net improvement.
